captions.linkedin:
Don't trade the FX carry until you understand the August 2007 chart.

Carry isn't free yield. It's an insurance premium you're paid to absorb crash risk. Get the model wrong and you'll blow up the same month everyone else does.

The strategy is from Lustig, Roussanov and Verdelhan, Review of Financial Studies (2011). They formalized why carry returns look like a free lunch most months and a black hole on a few.

Here's the complete logic, no black box:

🔹 FORWARD-DISCOUNT SORT. Sort G10 and liquid EM currencies into 5 or 6 portfolios by interest-rate differential vs USD.
🔹 BASKET LONG-SHORT. Long the highest forward-discount basket, short the lowest. Equal-weight inside each basket.
🔹 MONOTONIC BETA. HML-FX betas rise from roughly 0 at low-carry to roughly 0.9 at high-carry. That monotonic slope is the signature of a risk factor.
🔹 CRASH-RISK PREMIUM. High-carry currencies depreciate sharply in risk-off. Returns load negatively on global FX-volatility shocks. (Menkhoff et al. 2012, JF.)
🔹 MONTHLY REBALANCE. Use 1-month forwards.
🔹 UNWIND CLUSTERING. Many small gains, occasional large losses. August 2007. October 2008. 2011. The model predicts the clustering.

Source: Lustig, Roussanov, Verdelhan (2011), Review of Financial Studies 24(11). Educational use only.

Post-2008 the premium compressed in developed markets and concentrated in EM. Watch CIP basis before you lever it.
